page: Amazon Web Services x8g.16xlarge is a memory-optimized server instance powered by custom AWS Graviton Neoverse-V2 processors. Operating on the arm64 architecture, this instance provides 64 dedicated physical cores running at 2.8 GHz with a single thread per core. The memory configuration consists of 1024.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high resource density of 16.0 GB per core. It features 64 KB of L1d cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 36 MB of L3 cache. The instance runs on the Nitro hypervisor and includes a 30 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, though it lacks local NVMe storage and bundled public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data highlights the memory subsystem and multi-core capabilities of this instance. Memory bandwidth tests show top-tier performance, reaching 7395.63 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 456.97 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. Multi-core performance is strong, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 109163.03 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 25533.0. Database operations and key-value store performance are notable, with PassMark database operations scoring in the top tier and Redis SET operations achieving 132.1 million operations per second. Single-core performance remains average to strong, as indicated by a Geekbench single-core score of 1888.0.

The arm64 architecture offers high memory density and efficient multi-core scaling, making it qualitatively cost-effective for memory-bound workloads compared to traditional x86 alternatives. However, the lack of local storage requires relying on network-attached storage, which may introduce latency tradeoffs. The absence of a GPU limits its utility for heavy parallel training, though it achieves strong text generation speeds of 40.99 tokens/sec on medium 7B LLM models. This instance is suited for large-scale in-memory databases, Redis caching layers, high-throughput web serving, and software compilation pipelines.
